answerChoices.label: Upfront resection with venous reconstruction
answerChoices.rationale: This potentially reconstructable venous pattern is not a simple clearly resectable relationship. Neoadjuvant therapy and reassessment are generally favored over proceeding directly to a technically complex operation.

answerChoices.label: Neoadjuvant chemotherapy with surgical reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The venous abnormality with preserved adjacent segments and separated arteries supports a potentially reconstructable borderline pattern. Begin systemic treatment, then reassess staging and technical resectability.

answerChoices.label: Palliative chemotherapy with response assessment
answerChoices.rationale: Venous involvement alone does not establish permanent unresectability. The supplied negative distant staging and potentially reconstructable local pattern retain a possible resection pathway.

decisionNodes.explanation: The venous contour change and short narrowed segment suggest borderline local anatomy rather than either a clear surgery-first relationship or necessarily permanent unresectability. Neoadjuvant systemic treatment with restaging and surgical reassessment is the best offered sequence. Patency above and below supports consideration of reconstruction; it does not guarantee technical feasibility, which requires specialist review.

decisionNodes.currentUpdate: The multidisciplinary team plans several cycles of preoperative chemotherapy for the pancreatic-head adenocarcinoma. decisionNodes.stem: Which pre-treatment management plan is best for {patientName} at this visit?

answerChoices.label: ERCP metal stenting before chemotherapy
answerChoices.rationale: Obstructive jaundice should be relieved before the planned neoadjuvant course. A self-expanding metal stent offers more durable drainage through that treatment interval than a plastic stent.

answerChoices.label: ERCP plastic stenting before chemotherapy
answerChoices.rationale: Plastic stenting can decompress the duct but is more prone to occlusion during a prolonged neoadjuvant interval. The planned course makes durable metal-stent drainage preferable here.

answerChoices.label: Begin chemotherapy with bilirubin reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The patient has progressive obstructive jaundice before a multi-cycle course. Reassessment alone does not first relieve the obstruction or provide durable drainage.

decisionNodes.explanation: Progressive jaundice with upstream dilation represents clinically important biliary obstruction even without cholangitis. Drain it before the planned neoadjuvant course. Endoscopic self-expanding metal stenting is preferred to plastic stenting for durable drainage through that interval. This comparison does not establish one metal-stent design as universally best and does not create a numerical bilirubin rule.

fairness: The short irregular narrowed venous segment, patent vein above and below, absent arterial involvement and negative distant staging support the intended borderline rather than clearly resectable or permanently unresectable interpretation. The real competing error is equating potentially reconstructible venous involvement with an automatic surgery-first indication. Anatomy must first be interpreted and then applied to treatment sequence; the surgical and palliative alternatives are clinically meaningful.

No confident clinical inaccuracy identified. The explanation properly avoids claiming that patency guarantees reconstruction. Exact anatomic classification and technical feasibility remain matters for specialist/clinician review; no unsupported angle threshold is required here.

record.title: Biliary drainage before a neoadjuvant treatment course
fairness: Progressive symptomatic obstructive jaundice before several cycles of chemotherapy favors drainage; the anticipated course then favors a metal rather than plastic stent among these choices. Deferring drainage until infection develops and selecting a less durable stent are distinct credible errors.

Plastic stenting can drain obstruction and is not inherently wrong care, but it is a less appropriate preferred strategy for the stated prolonged preoperative course. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified; the explanation avoids a universal device-design claim or invented bilirubin cutoff.

The absence of fever does not remove the need to address the obstruction, and unaltered anatomy supports the offered endoscopic route. These are decision-relevant observations, not direct naming of the key.

The update supplies the diagnosis, planned treatment and new findings, so the task stands with the shared presentation without requiring the learner to have answered the preceding node correctly. That node's explanation does not teach metal versus plastic selection. No material wording-only cue identified.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan should have been recommended for {patientName} at this point in the hospital course?

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus image-guided catheter drainage
answerChoices.rationale: The existing catheter drains a different collapsed compartment. Persistent infection with a separate collection needs effective source control; image-guided access is the less invasive initial approach in this stable record.

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus interval imaging reassessment
answerChoices.rationale: The record contains ongoing infection with a separate undrained collection. The presence of an existing catheter does not establish source control when its side holes are confined to another compartment.

answerChoices.label: Antibiotics plus operative washout and drainage
answerChoices.rationale: Operative source control is a real option, but stable physiology without generalized peritonitis and an available image-guided approach favor a minimally invasive attempt first. This is not a requirement to delay surgery if the situation changes.

decisionNodes.explanation: The catheter's side holes are in the collapsed anterior space, while the infected-appearing collection occupies a separate posterior compartment. Antibiotics and the existing catheter have therefore not established adequate source control. Image-guided catheter drainage is the preferred initial addition in this stable hospital record. IR must choose new placement or exchange from the actual anatomy; the question does not promise that repositioning through the old tract will work. Operative drainage remains appropriate if interventional control fails or surgical indications develop.

exhibit.caption: Constructed teaching record; fictional patient observations
cells: Collapsed space containing all side holes of the existing catheter
Rim-enhancing fluid with internal gas, separated from the anterior space by tissue; posterior skin-to-collection path crosses no bowel or major vessel
No diffuse free air; no active hemorrhage

record.title: Source control for a separate undrained postoperative compartment
fairness: The resident must interpret the catheter side-hole and compartment relationship, then select an appropriate intervention level for persistent infection with stable circulation and no generalized peritonitis. Antibiotic reassessment and operative washout are real competing escalation choices.

Image-guided catheter source control is the best offered initial addition. The explanation avoids promising that an old tract can simply be repositioned and allows procedural planning or escalation according to actual findings. No confident clinical inaccuracy identified.

The skin-to-collection path is a favorable clue, but it is a concrete anatomic observation needed to judge a drainage route, not an assertion that 'IR is available' or an instruction to choose the key. It still requires knowledge of source-control strategy. Option wording is parallel, with antibiotics common to all choices.

The hospital-versus-current-clinic chronology is explicit and prevents interpreting a past acute intervention as an outpatient procedure. This revised node stands alone; no earlier diagnosis or management answer is required. Collection dimensions and the antibiotic interval are not given, but the stated persistent infection and separate undrained compartment support the offered ranking without inventing thresholds.

choices.choiceLabel: Antibiotics plus operative washout and drainage

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 67-year-old woman, attends clinic with worsening early fullness and vomiting after meals. MRI and EUS show a lobulated body cyst made of many tiny locules surrounding a central scar. It narrows the adjacent stomach; endoscopy shows intact mucosa at the indentation. She has no pancreatitis history and is fit for pancreatic surgery.

decisionNodes.stem: Which management plan best addresses {patientName}'s pancreatic lesion and current symptoms?

answerChoices.label: Continue pancreatic MRI surveillance
answerChoices.rationale: The phenotype is reassuring for malignancy, but surveillance does not address demonstrated symptomatic compression.

answerChoices.label: Arrange endoscopic cystgastrostomy
answerChoices.rationale: A microcystic epithelial lesion is not an inflammatory collection that can be treated by cystgastrostomy.

answerChoices.label: Refer for pancreatic cyst resection
answerChoices.rationale: A convincingly serous lesion can still require surgery when it causes adjacent-organ compression and symptoms.

decisionNodes.explanation: The microcystic, central-scar pattern favors a serous lesion. Usually benign behavior does not eliminate the mechanical indication: the lesion narrows the stomach and symptoms match that site. Resection evaluation is appropriate; a benign epithelial cyst is not managed as a pseudocyst.

concept.learningObjective: Recognize when a usually benign cyst phenotype has a mechanical indication for treatment.

record.title: Symptomatic serous-pattern cyst with gastric compression
fairness: The learner must recognize a likely benign serous phenotype and then distinguish benign biology from a symptomatic mechanical indication for surgery. Surveillance is a plausible error if benignity is overgeneralized.

The supplied gastric narrowing and concordant postprandial symptoms support resection evaluation. Cystgastrostomy is not appropriate treatment of the described epithelial cyst. The absence of a numerical size cutoff does not prevent this symptom-based decision.

The option lengths and categories are reasonably parallel, and the task is complete. The central-scar pattern is legitimate diagnostic evidence, not a verbatim answer label. No confident clinical inaccuracy or nonmedical answer shortcut identified.

case.presentation: {patientName}, a 64-year-old woman, attends clinic to review her outside distal-pancreatectomy records. Pathology shows IPMN with low-grade dysplasia and no invasive carcinoma. The pancreatic margin contains low-grade dysplasia. MRI of the remnant shows a small side-branch cyst with no mural nodule or main-duct dilation. She remains fit for further treatment if a future indication develops.

decisionNodes.stem: Which pancreatic-remnant management plan should be recommended for {patientName} now?

answerChoices.label: Completion pancreatectomy
answerChoices.rationale: Low-grade margin dysplasia and an unconcerning remnant cyst do not establish a need to remove the remaining pancreas.

answerChoices.label: MRI-based surveillance of the pancreatic remnant
answerChoices.rationale: Resected IPMN still warrants remnant surveillance; the low-grade margin and low-risk remnant do not by themselves select completion surgery.

answerChoices.label: Discharge from pancreatic imaging follow-up
answerChoices.rationale: The absence of invasive cancer does not remove the remnant risk associated with IPMN.

decisionNodes.explanation: Low-grade IPMN at a margin is not equivalent to invasive cancer at a margin. With no concerning remnant finding, surveillance preserves the opportunity to detect later disease without automatic completion pancreatectomy. Postresection IPMN follow-up differs from a completely resected noninvasive MCN.

question.explanation: Low-grade IPMN at a margin is not equivalent to invasive cancer at a margin. With no concerning remnant finding, surveillance preserves the opportunity to detect later disease without automatic completion pancreatectomy. Postresection IPMN follow-up differs from a completely resected noninvasive MCN.

concept.displayName: Preserve appropriate remnant surveillance without treating low-grade IPMN margins as an automatic completion-resection indication.
concept.learningObjective: Preserve appropriate remnant surveillance without treating low-grade IPMN margins as an automatic completion-resection indication.

record.title: Low-grade IPMN margin and pancreatic-remnant surveillance
fairness: The learner must interpret low-grade dysplasia at a margin differently from invasive or high-grade disease, then preserve remnant surveillance despite the absence of invasive carcinoma. Completion pancreatectomy and discharge represent distinct, recognizable over- and undertreatment errors.

Surveillance is the best offered plan for this fit patient with low-grade margin dysplasia and no concerning remnant imaging feature. The retained remnant cyst also makes discontinuing imaging a poor answer here.
The explanation appropriately distinguishes resected IPMN from completely resected noninvasive MCN and does not invent a surveillance interval or cancer probability.

The task is complete, options are parallel management strategies, and no preceding node is needed. No confident clinical inaccuracy or answer-selecting wording shortcut identified; exact surveillance-policy details still require clinician review.

claims.statement: Suspected adult blunt cardiac injury requires ECG and troponin I assessment; CK-MB does not replace either component.
claims.limitation: Single guideline for the exact management rule; no universal assay cutoff or serial schedule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: A post-trauma ECG change or elevated troponin I supports cardiac monitoring; baseline ECG comparison matters.
claims.limitation: Single 2012 guideline; an abnormal screen does not identify a particular structural lesion.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Routine echocardiography is not the initial screening strategy for every hemodynamically stable blunt-chest-injury patient.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; elevated biomarkers require monitoring and clinical reassessment, and new symptoms may change the imaging indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Cardiac CT or MRI may help distinguish traumatic cardiac injury from infarction in selected patients after initial evaluation.
claims.limitation: Level 3 recommendation; not a substitute for the acute indicated bedside echocardiogram.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Persistent new arrhythmia or hemodynamic instability after blunt chest trauma warrants echocardiography.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; the related inadequate-TTE claim specifies when TEE follows. No routine TEE for every screened patient.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: When echocardiography is indicated after blunt chest trauma but an adequate transthoracic study cannot be obtained, TEE is the supported next modality.
claims.limitation: Single guideline. No esophageal contraindication or new imaging technology eligibility rule is invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Normal ECG and troponin I remove the BCI monitoring indication in the EAST pathway without resolving other admission needs.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; timing remains unsettled and this does not claim perfect universal diagnostic sensitivity.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: A sternal fracture does not independently mandate cardiac monitoring when ECG and troponin I are normal.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; other chest-injury needs remain.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Analgesia, coughing support and respiratory rehabilitation address impaired breathing after traumatic chest-wall injury.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline; no invented spirometry admission threshold, analgesic regimen or automatic level of care.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: An inadvertently organ-traversing chest tube should stay in place pending urgent cross-sectional assessment and controlled multidisciplinary management.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline. No removal technique, exact vascular procedure, numeric stability threshold or new clinical probability is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

verificationBySource.verificationRole: Targeted primary guidance; case observations constructed.

claims.statement: Ongoing thoracic hemorrhage with hemodynamic instability warrants operative control even when drain output understates the blood loss.
claims.limitation: Current and older society guidance agree that physiology outweighs output alone. Constructed drain observations are not new volume thresholds.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Unstable thoracic vascular bleeding favors open exploration, whereas suitable stable arterial injuries may permit endovascular treatment.
claims.limitation: Single current guideline; no universal competition between all open/hybrid approaches or unverified device eligibility.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Thoracoscopy can manage selected residual hemothorax or bleeding in a hemodynamically stable trauma patient.
claims.limitation: Single guideline. This does not make VATS the appropriate first access during resuscitation-dependent shock.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Substantial retained traumatic hemothorax after tube drainage favors early VATS over thrombolysis in an operative candidate.
claims.limitation: EAST conditional, very-low-quality evidence, update in process. Exact early boundary in EAST is at most four days; draft supplies hospital day three without claiming a universal deadline.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Residual traumatic pleural blood can contribute to empyema and fibrothorax.
claims.limitation: Older guideline used for the general complication relationship; no incidence, deadline or probability authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Persistent respiratory impairment with displaced rib injuries despite multimodal and regional analgesia supports considering rib stabilization.
claims.limitation: Thresholds in PS 1.2 directly verified; draft uses multiple severely displaced ipsilateral ribs and failed ventilator liberation. Stabilization is a specialist assessment, not a guaranteed outcome.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Pulmonary contusion does not automatically exclude an otherwise appropriate patient from rib stabilization assessment.
claims.limitation: Individualized surgical assessment remains necessary; the draft does not treat contusion as evidence that fixation is automatically beneficial.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with the specified thoracic injury in outside-hospital records reviewed in clinic.

claims.statement: Tracheostomy may support prolonged ventilatory care but does not reconstruct displaced ribs.
claims.limitation: The counterfactual describes treatment purpose, not an exact tracheostomy timing or automatic indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the explicitly described outside-hospital trauma setting.

claims.statement: Men age 65 through 75 who have ever smoked should receive one-time abdominal ultrasound screening for abdominal aortic aneurysm.
claims.limitation: Exact pre-existing atomic statement and stable claim ID retained; source mapping freshly verified. Limited to asymptomatic previously unscreened men; not a diagnostic strategy for symptoms.
claims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic men 65-75 with previous tobacco use and no completed abdominal aortic screen.

claims.statement: A scan ending near the celiac origin does not assess the infrarenal abdominal aorta.
claims.limitation: Underlying aortic segment relationships independently synthesized from the official anatomy/segment definitions; no figure copied.
claims.applicablePopulation: Interpreting the inferior boundary of a thoracoabdominal acquisition.

claims.statement: Symptoms attributable to an intact AAA warrant repair assessment regardless of usual asymptomatic diameter thresholds.
claims.limitation: Pain attribution requires clinical assessment; no universal numeric pain or observation interval is supplied.
claims.applicablePopulation: Symptomatic intact AAA.

claims.statement: Attachment-site flow into an excluded sac represents a sealing failure.
claims.limitation: Type I origin; one directly checked specialty standard.
claims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR sac opacification.

claims.statement: An established type I endoleak warrants prompt correction of the seal.
claims.limitation: Cuff extension requires an available healthy landing segment; complex cases may need other repair. One directly checked publication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Persistent or late attachment leak.

claims.statement: An isolated type II endoleak with stable sac size can undergo imaging follow-up.
claims.limitation: Single publication; requires exclusion of higher-pressure leaks and continued surveillance.
claims.applicablePopulation: Asymptomatic patients with stable post-EVAR sac.

claims.statement: Retrograde flow from aortic side branches can fill the excluded sac.
claims.limitation: Type II physiology; other inflow sources must be assessed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Post-EVAR branch-associated flow.

claims.statement: Sac enlargement with uncertain leak origin requires investigation for occult type I or III inflow.
claims.limitation: Catheter angiography with possible cone-beam CT can resolve inconclusive CTA; no disputed growth cutoff is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Enlarging post-EVAR sac.

claims.statement: Ascending aortic involvement establishes type A dissection even with a distal entry tear.
claims.limitation: Classification depends on extent, not simply the tear location.
claims.applicablePopulation: Aortic dissection extending retrograde.

claims.statement: Acute type A dissection requires emergency surgical evaluation and immediate repair.
claims.limitation: Single checked multisociety guideline. This draft does not rank contested mesenteric-first strategies.
claims.applicablePopulation: Operable acute ascending dissection.

claims.statement: Acute type B dissection with organ malperfusion warrants intervention, commonly TEVAR when suitable.
claims.limitation: Static branch disease can require adjuncts; no automatic bowel resection or non-aneurysm ischemia objective is included.
claims.applicablePopulation: Complicated acute type B dissection.

claims.statement: Uncomplicated acute type B dissection initially receives medical therapy and close monitoring.
claims.limitation: High-risk morphology and later complications can change the plan; does not ban elective later TEVAR.
claims.applicablePopulation: Acute descending dissection without rupture or malperfusion.

claims.statement: Use intravenous beta blockade first, adding intravenous vasodilation if pressure remains high.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked recommendation; contraindications can favor a non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker. No dose or numeric target is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hypertensive acute aortic syndrome without beta-blocker contraindication.

claims.statement: Acute aortic-syndrome therapy generally targets a heart rate of 60-80 beats per minute while maintaining organ perfusion.
claims.limitation: Single checked guideline; individual perfusion and contraindications govern treatment. No dose is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Monitored hospital treatment of acute aortic syndrome.

claims.statement: Intravenous nicardipine is an antihypertensive vasodilator that can be combined with beta blockade under monitoring.
claims.limitation: The regulatory label verifies pharmacology; ACC/AHA establishes adding vasodilation after initial beta blockade when pressure remains uncontrolled. No dose or infusion-rate rule is authored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Hospital blood-pressure treatment after initial impulse control.

claims.statement: An intravenous non-dihydropyridine calcium-channel blocker is a reasonable acute aortic-syndrome rate-control alternative when beta blockers are contraindicated or not tolerated.
claims.limitation: Single checked guideline. This is a rate-control alternative, not evidence that switching from tolerated beta blockade is preferred for persistent pressure elevation after rate control.
claims.applicablePopulation: Acute aortic syndrome with a beta-blocker contraindication or intolerance.

claims.statement: Planned left-subclavian coverage should account for a patent LIMA coronary graft by preserving its inflow.
claims.limitation: Elective setting with native landing zones; bypass versus transposition depends on anatomy.
claims.applicablePopulation: TEVAR involving LSA with LIMA-dependent myocardium.

claims.statement: Carotid-subclavian transposition requires temporary proximal subclavian clamping.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; the anatomy-specific interruption matters for a pedicled LIMA.
claims.applicablePopulation: Open subclavian transposition.

claims.statement: A patent pedicled LIMA coronary graft favors bypass over subclavian transposition to avoid interrupting coronary inflow.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline, section on LSA revascularization; other bypass/endovascular configurations remain specialist decisions.
claims.applicablePopulation: LSA revascularization with a patent pedicled LIMA.

claims.statement: New spinal-cord dysfunction after TEVAR calls for perfusion rescue, including pressure support and CSF drainage assessment.
claims.limitation: Rapid specialist response; drainage contraindications must be checked. No invented target, timing, guaranteed recovery or routine prophylactic drain rule.
claims.applicablePopulation: Post-TEVAR neurologic deficit.

claims.statement: A small PAA with thrombus and distal embolic findings merits repair consideration despite being below 20 mm.
claims.limitation: Single guideline, weak recommendation/low-quality evidence; excludes acutely threatened limbs requiring an ischemia-specific pathway.
claims.applicablePopulation: PAA under 20 mm with embolic findings.

claims.statement: Finding a PAA warrants screening the opposite popliteal artery and abdominal aorta.
claims.limitation: Single guideline, strong recommendation/moderate evidence; this is aneurysm screening, not broad asymptomatic arterial-stenosis screening.
claims.applicablePopulation: Patients with a diagnosed PAA.

claims.statement: Open repair is preferred for an intact TAAA requiring repair in Marfan syndrome.
claims.limitation: Single directly checked guideline; does not preclude endovascular rescue or exceptional high-risk situations. Newer ESVS full text was inaccessible.
claims.applicablePopulation: Fit patient with heritable native-aorta TAAA.

claims.statement: Unexplained infection or gastrointestinal bleeding after aortic grafting warrants cross-sectional graft evaluation.
claims.limitation: Single guideline; imaging and cultures are interpreted together, and an unrevealing endoscopy does not assess the graft.
claims.applicablePopulation: Prosthetic aortic graft with unexplained infection/bleeding.

claims.statement: In an at-risk cirrhotic liver, a new solid lesion larger than 1 cm is characterized using dedicated multiphasic contrast CT or MRI.
claims.limitation: One adequate newly retrieved publication supports this fact; no independent direct corroboration is claimed.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: A suspicious lesion remaining uncharacterized after adequate dynamic imaging may require biopsy to establish tumor type before treatment.
claims.limitation: Supports persistent indeterminacy here, not routine biopsy of every lesion or of classic HCC imaging.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: A subcentimeter nodule detected during HCC surveillance can follow close imaging surveillance rather than the immediate diagnostic pathway used for a larger solid lesion.
claims.limitation: No exact surveillance interval is taught. Applies to the stated at-risk surveillance setting, without another supplied concerning finding.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: In cirrhosis, a lesion at least 2 cm with nonrim arterial hyperenhancement and nonperipheral washout can satisfy an imaging diagnosis of HCC.
claims.limitation: Applies to adequate multiphasic examinations in the appropriate at-risk population; no imaging diagnosis for an arbitrary noncirrhotic mass.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

claims.statement: A malignant-appearing liver observation with rim arterial enhancement in an at-risk liver requires tissue classification because it is not specific for HCC.
claims.limitation: AASLD recommends biopsy for LR-M observations; this is not a universal preoperative-biopsy rule for every suspected resectable cholangiocarcinoma.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

claims.statement: Biopsy is not routinely required solely to establish the diagnosis of an imaging-characteristic HCC, although an independent tissue or molecular indication may justify sampling.
claims.limitation: Multidisciplinary decisions can favor tissue even for LR-5 observations. The minimum-required-sampling task excludes a trial or separate molecular-tissue indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing multidisciplinary liver-tumor evaluation and major-hepatectomy planning.

claims.statement: Solitary localized HCC with preserved hepatic reserve and no clinically significant portal hypertension supports specialist resection assessment when remnant and anatomy are favorable.
claims.limitation: Cross-check of the existing favorable-profile claim. Portal hypertension is not asserted to prohibit every limited resection.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: A hepatic resection plan must preserve sufficient functioning liver with arterial and portal inflow, hepatic venous outflow and biliary drainage.
claims.limitation: Apply to the stated anatomy and care phase; patient-specific ranking requires clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: Thermal ablation provides more reliable local control for small HCC than for progressively larger lesions.
claims.limitation: Qualitative size-related suitability only; no universal procedure ranking or exact probability is taught.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: For the approved profile of a solitary HCC with preserved liver function, no clinically significant portal hypertension, adequate future liver remnant, and no macrovascular invasion or extrahepatic disease, hospital HPB-surgery referral for hepatic resection evaluation is the selected disposition.
claims.limitation: This is a deliberately favorable multiparametric profile, not a universal treatment rule for every solitary HCC or every person with Child-Pugh A cirrhosis. EASL 2025 metadata was not locally verifiable, so this package records the single-source limitation rather than inventing a second citation. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults represented by the owner-approved compensated-cirrhosis profiles in this package.

claims.statement: Clinically significant portal hypertension is one selection consideration in the approved favorable resection profile.
claims.limitation: This package does not teach clinically significant portal hypertension as an absolute contraindication to every limited hepatic resection, nor does it make preserved liver function alone sufficient for selection. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying only the clear favorable-profile boundary in the approved cases.

claims.statement: Limited HCC burden with decompensated cirrhosis supports transplant-center assessment rather than assuming a routine favorable resection pathway.
claims.limitation: Assessment is not guaranteed listing; one retrieved government summary directly corroborates the historical local decision.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: Meeting standard Milan criteria supports transplant-center evaluation but does not by itself guarantee listing or transplantation; disease outside Milan criteria may still warrant specialist evaluation of other pathways.
claims.limitation: This concept intentionally excludes AFP policy, downstaging selection, organ allocation, liver function, comorbid contraindications, and individualized treatment choice. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Learners applying standard Milan criteria without equating a tumor-burden classification with automatic listing or permanent exclusion.

claims.statement: HCC commonly draws substantial arterial flow while surrounding liver depends importantly on portal flow; arterial embolization with major portal obstruction can endanger hepatic function.
claims.limitation: NCI identifies portal-vein thrombosis as a relative TAE/TACE contraindication. This is not an absolute ban on every specialist-directed locoregional technique.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: Advanced HCC outside a suitable locoregional pathway warrants medical-oncology assessment for systemic treatment when hepatic function and general condition permit.
claims.limitation: No named systemic regimen, dose or first-line ranking is keyed. Current primary updates need targeted verification before such details are added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: Standard Milan classification requires no macrovascular invasion and no extrahepatic disease.
claims.limitation: Microscopic pathology, transplant-center assessment, tumor biology, and other candidacy factors are outside this narrow recognition concept. Offline reuse: source verification and currentness have not been refreshed for N1. Exact authored application and option ranking require clinician review. Only one recorded source supports this atomic claim; no independent management cross-check has been added.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults with confirmed hepatocellular carcinoma whose staging is being compared with standard Milan criteria.

claims.statement: TACE can be considered for nonmetastatic HCC unsuitable for surgery or ablation when hepatic perfusion and reserve permit.
claims.limitation: Not a universal treatment hierarchy, a fixed tumor cutoff or an assertion that all portal obstruction permits routine TACE.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults undergoing specialist assessment of hepatic malignancy.

claims.statement: Borderline pancreatic cancer commonly requires neoadjuvant systemic treatment and restaging rather than immediate surgery.
claims.limitation: Venous reconstructibility and local criteria require expert review. No universal neoadjuvant rule for clearly resectable disease is scored.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Reconstructible portal/mesenteric venous involvement need not make pancreatic cancer permanently unresectable.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Distant metastatic pancreatic adenocarcinoma ordinarily calls for systemic treatment rather than curative pancreatic resection.
claims.limitation: Exceptional oligometastatic research strategies are not a routine resection indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Obstructive jaundice before neoadjuvant therapy is an indication for biliary drainage; endoscopic covered metal stenting is preferred to plastic stenting in the verified consensus.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified ranking; no duration, bilirubin cutoff or metal-stent subtype superiority beyond that guidance is invented.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: During pancreatic-cancer neoadjuvant therapy, metal biliary stents have lower recurrent obstruction and reintervention rates than plastic stents in comparative pooled evidence.
claims.limitation: Heterogeneous comparative studies; no numerical effect, bilirubin cutoff, fixed chemotherapy interval, universal metal-design preference or guaranteed freedom from obstruction is inferred.
claims.applicablePopulation: Only the stated adult clinic consultation and proposed specialist investigations; no acute hypoglycemia rescue or MEN1 operative-extent algorithm is tested.

claims.statement: A pancreatic postoperative infected collection often requires antibiotics and effective interventional drainage.
claims.limitation: Single verified review; source-control approach depends on anatomy and stability. No invented antibiotic regimen.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Reoperation or completion pancreatectomy is generally reserved for failure of conservative/interventional treatment or a complication that requires surgery.
claims.limitation: Single verified review. Preserve instability, peritonitis and failed-access boundaries.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A convincingly serous cyst causing adjacent-organ compression can warrant resection despite its usually benign behavior.
claims.limitation: Single directly verified current position paper; asymptomatic size alone does not establish this indication.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A microcystic pancreatic lesion with a central scar supports a serous-cyst phenotype.
claims.limitation: Imaging is suggestive rather than definitive histology; atypical lesions need further characterization.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Imaging suggests cyst subtype but cannot establish histology or exclude malignancy.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Pancreatic-remnant surveillance remains indicated after IPMN resection, including noninvasive disease.
claims.limitation: Independently synthesized guideline fact; exact application remains subject to named clinical review.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: Low-grade dysplasia at an IPMN resection margin does not by itself require completion pancreatectomy.
claims.limitation: Single targeted international guideline; surveillance and individual cancer risk still matter. Exact margin question checked against European 2018 historical guidance, which is not used as a new reusable corpus.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.

claims.statement: A completely resected MCN without associated pancreatic cancer does not require postoperative cyst surveillance under ACG guidance.
claims.limitation: This applies to confirmed completely resected noninvasive MCN, not presumed imaging-only MCN or IPMN.
claims.applicablePopulation: Adults in the stated pancreatic clinic or outside-hospital chart-review scenario; no extrapolation to all pancreatic lesions.
